sentences.text: If a current is pushing you sideways and you point straight at your destination, you’ll miss it.
So you aim off, upstream, by just the right amount.
Finding that amount is called current sailing.
Look at the diagram, and follow the three steps.
First, draw your intended track, from where you are to where you want to go.
Second, from your starting point, draw the current: its set, and its drift for one hour.
Third, from the end of that current line, swing an arc equal to your boat speed for one hour, until it cuts your intended track.
The line from the end of the current to that crossing point is your course to steer.
And the distance from your start to that crossing point, along the track, is your speed made good.
We’ll draw these for real in the plotting module.
